pharm: Selectively antagonizes the endothelin-A (ETA) receptor on vascular smooth muscle, blocking endothelin-1-mediated vasoconstriction and cell proliferation in the pulmonary vasculature
quick: 5 mg once daily; titrate at 4-week intervals to 10 mg; max with cyclosporine is 5 mg/day
With or without food; do not split, crush, or chew tablets
Contraindicated - boxed warning for embryo-fetal toxicity (REMS); exclude pregnancy first
Choose either the drug or breastfeeding (not both)
No specific adjustment; elimination is predominantly non-renal
Not recommended in moderate or severe hepatic impairment
Hemoglobin, peripheral edema/fluid status, pregnancy tests (females)
summary: Ambrisentan (Letairis) is a selective endothelin-A receptor antagonist indicated for treatment of pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH, WHO Group 1) in adults to improve exercise ability and delay clinical worsening, and in combination with tadalafil to reduce disease progression and PAH hospitalization. It carries a boxed warning for embryo-fetal toxicity and historically was available only through a REMS. Dosing starts at 5 mg once daily, titrated to 10 mg; it is contraindicated in pregnancy and idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis.
indications: Pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH, WHO Group 1) in adults, to improve exercise ability and delay clinical worsening
In combination with tadalafil, to reduce the risks of disease progression and hospitalization for worsening PAH and to improve exercise ability

dosage.d: Start 5 mg once daily (with or without tadalafil 20 mg once daily); at 4-week intervals, increase ambrisentan to 10 mg (or tadalafil to 40 mg) as needed and tolerated
dosage.n: Do not split, crush, or chew tablets

dosage.d: Limit ambrisentan to 5 mg once daily

dosage.n: Not studied; avoid in moderate-severe hepatic impairment

admin: Take orally once daily, with or without food
Swallow whole - do not split, crush, or chew tablets
May be started together with tadalafil
Females: exclude pregnancy before starting and use effective contraception (REMS requirements historically applied)
moa: Endothelin-1 (ET-1) is a potent vasoconstrictor whose effects are mediated by ETA and ETB receptors; ETA primarily mediates vasoconstriction and cell proliferation. In PAH, plasma and lung ET-1 are markedly increased and correlate with disease severity. Ambrisentan is a high-affinity ETA receptor antagonist (Ki = 0.011 nM) with high selectivity for ETA over ETB (>4000-fold); the clinical impact of this high selectivity is not known.

absolute: Idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF), including IPF patients with pulmonary hypertension (WHO Group 3)
relative: Moderate or severe hepatic impairment (use not recommended)
Pre-existing fluid overload / decompensated heart failure (fluid retention risk)
monitor: Hemoglobin at initiation, at 1 month, and periodically
Signs of fluid retention / peripheral edema
Pregnancy tests in females of reproductive potential

preg: BOXED WARNING - embryo-fetal toxicity. Ambrisentan is contraindicated in pregnancy; based on animal data it may cause fetal harm including major birth defects and fetal death (teratogenic in rats and rabbits). Exclude pregnancy before initiation, advise effective contraception before, during, and for one month after treatment, and discontinue as soon as pregnancy is detected. Females access historically required enrollment in a REMS program.
lact: There are no data on the presence of ambrisentan in human milk, the effects on the breastfed infant, or effects on milk production. Because of potential serious adverse reactions, a patient should choose either ambrisentan or breastfeeding, but not both.
renal: No specific renal dose adjustment is described; elimination of ambrisentan is predominantly by non-renal pathways. Dose adjustment based on renal impairment is generally not required per labeling.
hepatic: Ambrisentan is not recommended in patients with moderate or severe hepatic impairment (not studied). Monitor for liver injury and avoid use when hepatic function is significantly impaired.

moderate: Cyclosporine - approximately doubles ambrisentan exposure; limit ambrisentan to 5 mg once daily
minor: Ambrisentan is a substrate of P-gp, OATP1B1/1B3 and is metabolized by CYP3A, CYP2C19, and UGTs; interactions possible but only cyclosporine has shown clinical relevance
interactions.food: Food does not affect bioavailability; may be taken with or without food
interactions.diagnostics: Monitor hemoglobin; pregnancy testing required in females of reproductive potential

serious: Clinically significant fluid retention / worsening heart failure
Pulmonary edema in patients with pulmonary veno-occlusive disease
emergency: Acute pulmonary edema (consider underlying pulmonary veno-occlusive disease)
Decompensated heart failure from fluid retention

monitoring: Hemoglobin at initiation, at about 1 month, and periodically thereafter
Peripheral edema and signs of fluid retention
Pregnancy tests before treatment in females of reproductive potential
counsel: Take one tablet once a day at about the same time; swallow whole and do not split, crush, or chew it
Report swelling of the legs/ankles, rapid weight gain, or increasing breathlessness
Females: this medicine can seriously harm an unborn baby - use effective contraception and take pregnancy tests as directed; stop and call your clinician if you may be pregnant
Tell your clinician about liver disease and any anemia symptoms (tiredness, paleness)
Do not breastfeed while taking this medicine
pk: Vasodilatory effect develops with dosing; clinical benefit over weeks
Peak plasma concentrations about 2 hours after oral dosing; food does not affect bioavailability
Terminal half-life ~15 hours; effective half-life ~9 hours
Once-daily dosing; accumulation factor about 1.2 at steady state
Store at 25 C (77 F); excursions permitted 15-30 C (59-86 F); keep in original packaging
pearls: Boxed warning for embryo-fetal toxicity; exclude pregnancy and mandate effective contraception (historically dispensed through a REMS)
Selective ETA antagonist; contraindicated in pregnancy and in idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (including WHO Group 3 PH with IPF)
Peripheral edema and decreased hemoglobin are class effects of endothelin receptor antagonists - monitor hemoglobin at baseline, 1 month, and periodically
Limit dose to 5 mg daily with cyclosporine (exposure roughly doubles)
Not recommended in moderate to severe hepatic impairment
missed: If a dose is missed, take it as soon as remembered the same day, then resume the usual once-daily schedule. If it is nearly time for the next dose, skip the missed dose; do not take two doses to make up for a missed one.
overdose: There is no experience with overdose. The highest single dose in healthy volunteers was 100 mg; single 50 mg and 100 mg doses (5 to 10 times the maximum recommended dose) caused headache, flushing, dizziness, nausea, and nasal congestion. Massive overdose could potentially cause hypotension that may require intervention; provide supportive care.
